card.name: Sirius
card.kind: Star · Canis Major, the Great Dog
says: The brightest star of the night sky. A white star, hotter than the Sun. It shines with the light of 23 Suns.
8.6 light-years away: the light you see tonight left it in 2017.
That day it rose at 02:43 in the east-south-east, stood highest at 08:20, 54° up, set at 13:57 in the west-south-west.
At 10:00, the hour this sky is made for, Sirius stood 46° up in the south-west, hidden in daylight.
card.btn: Show Canis Major, the Great Dog

card.name: Moon
says: 43% lit and waning at this moment. 370,765 km away that day.
That day the Moon rose at 23:56, stood highest at 05:48, set at 12:41.
At 10:00, the hour this sky is made for, the Moon stood 34° up in the west-north-west.

card.name: Jupiter
says: Shining at magnitude -1.8 at this moment, brighter than almost every star.
That day Jupiter rose at 04:10, stood highest at 10:40, 88° up, set at 17:06.
At 10:00, the hour this sky is made for, Jupiter stood 80° up in the east-south-east, hidden in daylight.

card.name: Vega
says: The 5th brightest star of the night sky. A white star, hotter than the Sun. It shines with the light of 50 Suns.
25 light-years away: the light you see tonight left it in 2001.
That day it rose at 13:02 in the north-east, stood highest at 20:09, 71° up, set at 03:17 in the north-west.
At 10:00, the hour this sky is made for, Vega was below the horizon, 26° down in the north-north-east.
